title: Longitudinal Investigation of Weight and Migraine With Atogepant in Clinical Obesity Settings
official: Longitudinal Investigation of Weight and Migraine With Atogepant in Clinical Obesity Settings
summary:
This interventional study aims to learn how atogepant, a medication approved to prevent migraines, affects migraine and body weight in adults who have both migraine and obesity.

The main questions are:

1. Is there a connection between starting atogepant and changes in migraine activity and body weight over time?
2. Do factors measured before starting atogepant help explain differences between people in how often they have migraines and how their weight changes, and how these two outcomes relate?
3. Do changing biological, behavioral, and psychological factors help explain how improvements in migraine relate to weight loss?

Participants will be followed for 44 weeks, with assessments at baseline, 12, 24, and 36 weeks. These assessments include 28 days of daily migraine activity tracking, daily weight measurements, behavioral monitoring, psychosocial questionnaires, biomarkers, and clinical/functional tests.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Overweight or obesity (BMI 25-55 kg/m2)
* Aged 18 to 70 years at the time of informed consent
* History of migraine for at least 1 year with or without aura consistent with the ICHD-3. (International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition)
* Migraine onset before age 50 years
* Willing and able to comply with all study requirements
* At least 3 headache days per month across the 3 months preceding formal screening/diagnosis

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindications to atogepant as indicated in the labeling
* Secondary headache disorder, as indicated by the SNNOOP10 Mnemonic for red flag symptoms and study neurologist judgment
* Current or prior use of atogepant
* Current use or planned use of other medications prescribed for migraine prevention or weight loss
* Plans to initiate or change the dosage or frequency of medications associated with weight loss, weight gain, or migraine frequency within one month prior study enrollment
* Chronic migraine with severe renal impairment and end-stage renal disease
* Any clinically significant disease (cardiovascular, hematologic, endocrine, pulmonary, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, neurologic) judged by the medical co-investigators to place the patient at significant risk
* Current pregnancy or plans to become pregnant
* Inability to read or understand the study materials
* Current participation in a structured weight management or headache management program
* Inability or unwillingness to complete the pre-treatment baseline assessment
* Any condition or plan that would hinder adherence to the study protocol (e.g., relocation, psychiatric problems such as substance abuse disorder)
* History of metabolic and bariatric surgery
